title: Test Coverage Conventions
description: Schema for test-coverage-conventions.json (bundled with the tdd-refactor-coverage-audit skill). The root is the STRICT entry point and requires 'languages'. The optional testCoverageAudit override block in framework-config.json validates against the LENIENT entry point at #/$defs/override, which shares the same property shapes but requires nothing — mergeConfig never reads override.languages, so requiring it would mandate a field the consumer discards (#286).

flowAnnotation.description: Top-level grammar for the tags a flow spec uses to declare what it covers. Top-level rather than per-language because the tags are the same wherever they appear; only the comment syntax around them differs.

readFrom.description: Where the reader looks. Only the leading comment block is recognised, so a tag deeper in the file is prose rather than a declaration.

excludePaths.description: Project-declared globs for paths that are not expected to have tests — golden files, fixture trees, generated sources, scratch directories. A matching source is neither counted nor reported as unpaired. Distinct from a language's excludePatterns, which says a file is not a source of THAT language; this says a path is not expected to be tested at all, whatever language claims it. Per-language pairing is untouched: a non-matching source in the same language still pairs and still reports as unpaired when it has no test.

override.description: Lenient entry point for the framework-config.json -> testCoverageAudit block. Same property shapes as the bundled conventions file, but no required fields: mergeConfig reads only additionalLanguages, ignoredSourcePatterns and minTestCoverageRatio.

flowTag.description: One recognised annotation tag. Constrained by pattern rather than enum for the same reason as testClass.pairing: the bundled validator implements pattern and not enum.

testClass.description: One test class within a language entry. `pairing` says how a test of this class is matched to what it exercises: 'stem' is filename-stem matching (today's behaviour, the module class), 'annotation' means the spec declares its subject in a leading-comment tag and filename is irrelevant, 'declared-subject' means the test names its subject and may instead match an `exempt` glob.

pairing.description: How this class pairs. Constrained by pattern rather than enum: the bundled validator in test-coverage-audit.js implements pattern and does not implement enum, so an enum here would validate nothing.

locations.description: Globs marking where tests of this class live. For the flow class this is what makes a spec eligible for annotation reading; it never pairs the spec by itself.

exempt.description: Globs whose members satisfy this class without a declared subject.

classes.description: Optional per-language test classes (module, flow, contract). A language declaring no classes block resolves to module-only behaviour, so existing entries are unaffected.

sourceExtensions.description: File extensions for source files in this language. Each must start with a dot, e.g. '.ts'.

testPatterns.description: Glob-like patterns for paired test files. Supports {stem} (filename without extension) and {dir} (relative directory of the source file).

excludePatterns.description: Glob patterns for source files to skip entirely.

inlineTests.description: If true, the audit checks the source file itself for an inline test block (e.g. Rust 'mod tests') before reporting missing tests.

pairingScope.description: Granularity of the pairing check. 'file' (default) requires a test matching testPatterns for this specific source file. 'directory' pairs a source when ANY file matching the language's test shape exists in the source's own directory — for languages whose idiom is one test file per package (Go). Coarser by design: one test file marks every source in its package paired.
